traits.leaf_width_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Glyceria elata: blades 6 mm to 1.2 cm wide.

traits.culm_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Glyceria elata: culms 1 m to 2 m tall.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: Hitchcock (1935), as Glyceria elata: panicle 15 cm to 30 cm long.

appearance.organs.panicle.note: The panicle's layout, the model's choice after FNA (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page was not read): pyramidal and open, its branches 12 to 17 cm, divergent to drooping, lax, each with 30 to 50 or more spikelets oval in side view. Drawn as 12 long branches leaning out and drooping, each with about 30 spikelets on its outer part, the spikelets 0.45 as wide as long (FNA: 1.5 to 2.8 mm wide). Colours by eye.

traits.note: FNA's account of the species (volume 24), as search results quote it (the page itself was not read): panicles 15 to 30 cm long and 12 to 30 cm wide, pyramidal, open, the branches 12 to 17 cm, divergent to drooping, lax, with 30 to 50 or more spikelets; spikelets 3 to 6 mm, oval in side view, with 3 to 4(6) florets; lower glumes 0.7 to 1.5 mm, upper 1 to 1.5 mm. The lemmas (1.7 to 2.2 mm) came only in the search results' own words; the genus has no awns.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a lush, tall grass of shaded wet ground with soft, flat blades and open, nodding panicles. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough sizes from general knowledge of the species: 1.2 m tall at 4 years in the open. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye: bright green blades; green panicles.

taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

provenance.notes: Procedural proxy from the step-6 catalogue, authored from general knowledge of the species in the south Puget Sound lowlands. Calibration against measurements and photographs is milestone P4.
